# Disability services and allied healthcare

Allied health practitioners are healthcare professionals who can help you take care of your physical or mental health.

Read below about the allied health practitioners, who work with people with disabilities, and the services they give. If you or someone you care for is with disability, learn how the National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIS) can help to support your access to these professionals and services.

#### Assistance dog

Assistance or service dogs are trained to help people living with disability. Find out more about assistance dogs, their training and NDIS funding on ...

Read more about Assistance dog.

#### Counsellors and counselling

If you are having difficulties in life, talking to a counsellor can help. Counsellors work in many areas, such as mental health, to provide advice.

Read more about Counsellors and counselling.

#### Cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT)

Cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) can help you to identify and check unhealthy or damaging thinking habits. Learn more about how CBT works.

Read more about Cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT).

#### Exercise physiologists

Exercise physiologists help improve your health through personalised exercise plans. Learn how they can help you and where to find one.

Read more about Exercise physiologists.

#### Guide dogs

Guide dogs, also called seeing eye dogs, are trained to help people who are blind or visually impaired to travel safely and independently.

Read more about Guide dogs.

#### Occupational therapy

Occupational therapists (OTs) can help throughout your life when you're having difficulty with everyday tasks. Learn about occupational therapy.

Read more about Occupational therapy.

#### Mobility aids

Mobility aids can help you get around and make daily activities safer and easier. Learn when you might need mobility aids and how to access them.

Read more about Mobility aids.

#### Paediatricians

Paediatricians provide care for babies, kids and teenagers. Ask them about childhood illnesses and physical, mental and behavioural development.

Read more about Paediatricians.

#### Physiotherapy

Physiotherapy can help treat a range of health problems. Learn about what physiotherapists do, the conditions they treat and how they can help you.

Read more about Physiotherapy.

#### Podiatrists

Podiatrists are foot and ankle experts who help prevent and treat various conditions. Learn about what a podiatrist does and how to find one.

Read more about Podiatrists.

#### Psychiatrists and psychologists

Psychiatrists and psychologists have advanced training in mental health. Learn what they do and who to call if you need help with your mental health.

Read more about Psychiatrists and psychologists.

#### Psychotherapy

Psychotherapy is a group of therapies to help you understand your thinking and behavioural patterns and improve your coping skills. Explore the types ...

Read more about Psychotherapy.

#### Social workers

Social workers can help if you have problems with your health, finances or living situation. Find out how a social worker may be able to help you.

Read more about Social workers.

#### Speech pathology

Speech pathologists help people with communication and swallowing problems. Learn more about speech pathologists, what they do and how they can help.

Read more about Speech pathology.
